verdict: Lend selectively in Guwahati logistics: pursue asset-backed warehousing and 3PL operators with clean receivables; avoid thin-margin trucking and receivables-heavy freight agents until collection cycles are verified.
title: Guwahati logistics & warehousing: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What this business physically is
**Logistics here is a cash-conversion business, not an asset business.** A Guwahati operator moves goods from railhead, river port and highway into godowns, then out to retail and e-commerce last mile; cash comes in per consignment or per pallet-day, and goes out in diesel, driver wages, rent and fuel advances. **The value sits in the warehouse lease and the route contract, not the truck.** So when a proposal lands, check whether the borrower owns or leases the shed, and who the anchor client is; if the client is a single e-commerce or FMCG account, ask for the contract tenure and termination clause.

## Where cash and value actually sit
**Working capital is the whole risk in this trade.** A peer's cycle stretched from 39 days in FY23 to 77 days in FY24 as collection period moved from 52 to 82 days against creditor days of five [10] — that is the shape of trouble. **Capex is heavy and debt-funded in this sector:** one rated peer ran ₹108 crore of debt-funded capex over FY2021 to H1 FY2024 with DSCR near 1.0 times [8], while a stronger peer held gearing at 0.22x with ₹72.08 crore of liquid funds [9]. So when a proposal lands, check debtor days against creditor days; if the gap is widening, ask for the top-five debtor ageing and the billing dispute log.

## What has changed now
**The national parcel cycle is expanding fast, and that pulls warehouse demand into Guwahati.** Delhivery's Q2 FY27 revenue from services was ₹3,066 crore, up 19.8% year-on-year, with express parcel shipments at 325 million, up 32.1% [3][4][5]; VRL reported Q1 FY27 revenue growth of 18% with EBITDA margin at 21.8% [6]. **Local sources are thin and dated:** the Guwahati supply-chain piece is from March 2024 [2] and the employment piece from November 2025 [1], so treat city-specific demand claims as indicative only and lean on first principles plus these peers.

## Early-warning signs
**Watch debtor days crossing creditor days, single-client concentration above half of billing, and capex funded by short-term working capital.** If a borrower's collection period moves past 82 days [10], ask for the client contract and stop enhancement. If DSCR sits near 1.0 times with fresh capex announced [8], ask for the promoter infusion plan before any new limit.
watch: crosses 82 days -> freeze enhancement, seek client contract
above 50% -> require assignment of receivables or co-obligation
near 1.0 times with new capex -> ask promoter infusion plan
gap above 10% -> stop disbursement, reconcile invoices
lease under 3 years or unregistered -> decline term loan
